messages.subject: weights to models ?
parts:
I want to do a weighted model in Stan - in the very old days, you just duplicated, triplicated etc, the samples that you regarded as more important( like recent samples versus older samples, or samples where the target was known to be less noisy that others ). Now R's lm  lets you provide a weights vector. 
For Stan after reading the discussion in the dev-group  - https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/stan-dev/5pJdH72hoM8
I tried this - 
      increment_log_prob(wtsnormedLogged[i]*normal_log(sess[i],(  p[i]  + weekly_tv*WEEKLY_TV_SPEND[i] + weekly_rd*WEEKLY_RD_SPEND[i] + tv_coeff*tv_spend_prime[i]
                                   + rd_coeff*rd_spend_prime[i]
                                   + br_coeff*SEM_BRAND_SPEND[i]
                                   + nb_coeff*SEM_NB_SPEND[i] ),sigma_sess));

And for the weights  I provided this via R ( code below is from R ) -  Since stan works in the logged space I thought I shd log the weights vector, in addition to normalising it to 1. I got Rhats of 10**5, 10**7 and so on !

Shdn't I be logging the wts vector then ? 

============= R code that creates the weighting vector
wts<-vector(length=(nrow(dms)))
wts<-c(rep(1,N_dates))
wts[as.Date(dms$Date)>as.Date('2014-12-08') & as.Date(dms$Date)<=as.Date('2015-01-05')]<-.0001
wts[as.Date(dms$Date)==as.Date('2015-12-25')]<-.00001
wts[dms$Year>=2016]<-30
total_wt<-sum(wts)
wtsnormed<-wts/total_wt
wtsnormedLogged<-log(wtsnormed)

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] weights to models ?
parts:
No, definitely not. Think about what happens when you
have two observations. You multiply their likelihoods
on the linear scale, so you add them on the log scale,
so that means you multiply the log likelihood by the weight
(which would be 2 in this case).

The new notation is

target += u;

instead of

increment_log_prob(u);

and normal_lpdf(y | mu, sigma) instead of normal_log(y, mu, sigma).

You should be using Stan 2.11 because there was a bug in 2.10
that got fixed (earlier releases are OK, but they haven't
been upgraded to the new notations that we're using going forward).

Having said all this, Andrew doesn't like the weighting because
it's not a generative model, but what you do with Stan is up to you!

- Bob

P.S. By "samples" you mean what we'd call observations
or modeled data (what is modeled by the likelihood or
sampling distribution---this terminology is all super confusing).

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] weights to models ?
parts:
On Tuesday, August 30, 2016 at 1:15:05 PM UTC-4, Shantanu K. Karve wrote:
Yup I saw that Andrew doesn't like weighting. I'll have to look up the term "generative model" to see what he's getting at

The idea is that the weights don't actually factor in to the data generating process (how the data came to be, so to speak). If you have a sample that you know isn't representative of the population then you can still use a generative model by conditioning on the relevant variables (i.e. the variables that would go into the weights).

returning to this - the thing about a Auto regressive model of some type i.e.

y(i) = f(  y(i-1), y(i-2)...  ) 
 where f is some linear function, is that there's nothing about regressors in there - it just says that my target/predicted variable depends on past values of itself.. 

I have regressors/ predictors so my equation is :
y(i)  = f(   g(x(i), x (i-1), x(i-2 )...   ) etc.. there's multiple predictors - advertising in print, radio, tv, digital etc.

 In this domain its called Adstock and saturation. The g function includes both a decay ( x'(i) = x(i) + lamba * x'(-1) )  and a saturation function which can be a power of less than 1 or a neg-exponential or logistic... Not sure if using such "moving average" of the predictors breaks any assumptions in stan..  

For some g's - I get good fit, good n_eff, Rhat, plots are fine. 

For others - which in business senses seem MORE sensible, I get really bad n_eff, Rhats and I would love to understand why. I can't get anything out of the Pairs plots yet.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] weights to models ?
parts:
> On Sep 15, 2016, at 2:27 PM, Shantanu K. Karve <shantan...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> returning to this - the thing about a Auto regressive model of some type i.e.
>
> y(i) = f( y(i-1), y(i-2)... )
> where f is some linear function, is that there's nothing about regressors in there - it just says that my target/predicted variable depends on past values of itself..
>
> I have regressors/ predictors so my equation is :
> y(i) = f( g(x(i), x (i-1), x(i-2 )... ) etc.. there's multiple predictors - advertising in print, radio, tv, digital etc.
>
> In this domain its called Adstock and saturation. The g function includes both a decay ( x'(i) = x(i) + lamba * x'(-1) ) and a saturation function which can be a power of less than 1 or a neg-exponential or logistic... Not sure if using such "moving average" of the predictors breaks any assumptions in stan..

The only assumptions we make are

1. that the program defines a proper density up to
an additive constant (i.e., the exp() of the log density
has a finite integral), and

2. the density is continuously differentiable.

Stan can run into sampling problems with too-fat tails, too-thin tails, or
extreme position-dependent curvature in the posterior.

Time series can have strong dependencies among the parameters,
which can sometimes be tackled by reparameterizing.

E.g., rather than

theta[t+1] ~ normal(theta[t], sigma);

you can use a non-centered parameterization with a parameter
theta_raw and transformed parameter theta, with


theta[t + 1] = theta[t] + sigma * theta_raw[t+1];

theta_raw[t + 1] ~ normal(0, 1);

The sampling will happen over the theta_raw, but you'll still
recover your theta.

- Bob
